thread:
maya: Quick sync — finalizing rollout approach for FP8/INT8/4-bit support. Need a concrete, ops-friendly plan that preserves user quality while letting us reclaim cost. TL;DR: shadow -> staged -> metric gates -> fallback. Thoughts?

ashwin: +1 on shadow first. We should run customer-specific shadow for 48h on a small traffic slice. capture: tokens, logits, topk diffs, latencies. keep it low-noise. :mag_right:

dina: Agree. Important: separate signal for hallucination-like regressions vs harmless token differences. We should instrument a "deg_score" per response (simple n-gram novelty + model-confidence delta to start).

cj: Operational constraints: Dedicated customers can't have noisy shadow on prod GPUs without explicit opt-in. Proposal: run shadow on dedicated customer's shadow fleet or on-hosted but labelled traffic. For hosted, we can do in-place.

maya: Good call. For dedicated customers default to "opt-in-shadow" and for hosted do opt-out if they signed the SLA (we already do this for other experiments).

ashwin: On thresholds: propose two-tier gates: quality gate and latency/cost gate. Quality gate: mean(deg_score) delta <= 0.03 and P(deg_score>0.12) < 1%. Latency gate: p95 latency delta <= 7% and 99th token tail not > 30ms extra. Cost gate: per-token CPU/GPU time delta within expected quant win +/- 10%.

dina: Those numbers seem reasonable as a starting point. We should also add an absolute fallback trigger: if any customer KPM (key prompts) set sees repeated failures (3/10 in a 5m window) rollback immediately.

cj: Implementation blockers: runtime needs an API flag: `quant.staged_profile=<name>` and `quant.shadow=true|false`. Also a `quant.rollback_reason` enum we populate. Ops wants these surfaced to Console.

maya: I'll file a small infra ticket for `quant.*` flags. Also we need a UI in Console to approve canaries per-customer.

ashwin: For canary percentages: start with 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 24-72h depending on signals. Each step must be gated by automated checks with a manual hold for major customers.

dina: For eval sets: create three tiers: SIMPLIFIED_PROMPTS (short chat), LONG_CONTEXT ( > 2k tokens), SENSITIVE_FACTS (legal/medical). Run both offline evals and in-shadow comparisons. We'll store diffs in a compact form (topk & token-level edit distance).

cj: Suggestion: add a "mini-corpus" per major customer (10-50 canonical prompts) to be used as a quality escrow during rollout. That way we can run deterministic daily checks.

maya: Yes. Product already has per-customer prompt capture opt-in; let's reuse that flow.

ashwin: Fallback hierarchy brainstorming: 1) intra-server runtime fallback to INT8/FP16 prequant profile, 2) route to alternate model variant (fp8-safe-vX), 3) route to hosted fallback pool (higher-cost) with existing precision, 4) fail closed (last resort). We need to pick order carefully to avoid latency spikes.

dina: Order looks right. But add step 0: transparent prefix caching — if output prefixes match cached responses we can short-circuit to avoid redoing inference. It helps latency-sensitive paths.

cj: Ops note: routing fallback to hosted pool must carry customer tenancy metadata and billing flags. Also SLA implications.

maya: What about aggressive per-token fallback? e.g., switch precision mid-generation if deg_score increases. Too risky?

ashwin: We explored per-token dynamic downgrade in the protos. Risk: KV cache format incompatibility + big perf cliff toggling back and forth. Prefer checkpoint boundaries (e.g., switch at generation chunk boundaries or on next request).

dina: Agreed. Also the quality telemetry is noisy per-token. Use session-level aggregation for decisions.

cj: Telemetry keys we need: `quant.profile`, `quant.applied_fallback`, `deg_score`, `sampling_temp`, `latency_token_ms`, `kv_cache_mismatch` flag. All should be indexed in the observability DB for quick pivots.

maya: We should predefine a small alert set: alert if P(deg_score>0.12) > 0.5% across canary for 30min OR latency p95 delta > 15% for 10min. Ops will trigger auto-rollback.

ashwin: For model builders: provide an automated `compare_generate` tool that runs baseline vs quant candidate on the same prompts and emits a compact diff bundle. Example usage: `./compare_generate --baseline=fp16 --candidate=fp8-compact --prompts=sample_set.json --out=diff.tgz`

dina: Also include a human-review workflow in Console: random sample of 200 responses from canary with side-by-side diffs and a 1-5 acceptability rating. This will help catch semantic shifts not captured by deg_score.

cj: Rollback playbook draft: 1) pause promotion, 2) flip `quant.staged_profile` back to previous, 3) surface incident in Console + slack incident channel with `rollback_reason`, 4) run root-cause bisect job (compare_generate on failing prompts), 5) schedule hotfix or revert.

maya: Who owns the bisect job? eng-ml for triage, but SRE/ops run the actual rollback ops.

ashwin: A final ask: we need to formalize the quality-contract for customers. Something like: "quantized variants are guaranteed to meet SLO X and quality delta Y; exceptions require explicit opt-in." Legal/product must sign off but we need a clear technical definition for Y (deg_score thresholds).

dina: I'll draft a short RFC appendix with the deg_score definition, thresholds, and eval suite. Will ping product for contract language.

ops-bot: Canary rollout started for `fp8-econ-v1` on hosted: 0.5% traffic, shadow=true, watchlist: maya, ashwin, dina.

maya: Thanks — will monitor. I'll create the infra ticket and a tracking PR for the Console UI. Proposed followups: (1) infra ticket for `quant.*` flags, (2) eval corpus + compare_generate CI job, (3) Console canary approval flow, (4) playbook + pager runbook. Anyone want to own docs?

ashwin: I'll own compare_generate CI + thresholds.

dina: I'll write the RFC appendix and the per-customer mini-corpus spec.

cj: I'll own ops rollbacks + Console integration requirements.

maya: Great. Closing this thread — pls put action items in the eng-ml board and assign. :white_check_mark:
